parts.official_mark_scheme_text: $\frac{dy}{dx}=2(x+1)-(x+1)^{-2}$. B1. Set $=0$ and obtain $2(x+1)^3=1$ convincingly, www AG. B1. $\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}=2+2(x+1)^{-3}$, www. B1. Substitute, e.g. $(x+1)^{-3}=2$ OE or $x=\left(\frac12\right)^{\frac13}-1$. M1. Requires exact method; otherwise scores M0. $\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}=6$ CAO, www. A1. Exact answer required; otherwise scores A0. Total: 5.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text: $y^2=(x+1)^4+(x+1)^{-2}+2(x+1)$ SOI. B1. OR $y^2=(x^4+4x^3+6x^2+4x+1)+(2x+2)+(x+1)^{-2}$. $(\pi)\int y^2\,dx=(\pi)\left[\frac{(x+1)^5}{5}+\frac{(x+1)^{-1}}{-1}+\frac{2(x+1)^2}{2}\right]$ OR $(\pi)\left(\left[\frac{x^5}{5}+x^4+2x^3+2x^2+x\right]+[x^2+2x]+\left[-\frac1{x+1}\right]\right)$. B1B1B1. Attempt to integrate $y^2$. Last term might appear as $(x^2+2x)$. $(\pi)\left[\frac{32}{5}-\frac12+4-\left(\frac15-1+1\right)\right]$. M1. Substitute limits $0\to1$ into an attempted integration of $y^2$. Do not condone omission of value when $x=0$. $9.7\pi$ or $30.5$. A1. Note: omission of $2(x+1)$ in first line $\to6.7\pi$ scores $3/6$. Ignore initially an extra volume, e.g. $(\pi)\int(4\frac12)^2$; only take into account for the final answer. Total: 6.
